//: case_d5cbfb18 tool_connection registration payload. Substitute MCP_HOSTNAME and
the secretId of the bearer, then create the connection with this config.
THE ONE FIELD THAT SILENTLY VOIDS THE WHOLE EPIC
config.headerPolicy.metadata.forward. The gateway derives its metadata
headers from this list and THE DEFAULT IS THE EMPTY LIST. A connection
registered the obvious way — url and nothing else, the Zapier pattern the
issue points at — forwards NO x-paperclip-agent-id, with no error, no
warning, and no degraded health status. The transport becomes silently
anonymous, which is the exact failure the epic exists to prevent.
Our server fails closed on a missing agent header, so the failure is loud
on the first tools/call rather than silent. That is a backstop, not a
reason to omit this list.
It must sit under `config`, not `transport_config`. readHeaderPolicy
checks config first and falls back to transportConfig; put it in config
and do not rely on the fallback.
NO SECRET IN THE URL
The existing Octavo Foundry / Zapier row carries its auth token in
plaintext in transport_config.url. That half of the pattern is
deliberately NOT copied. The bearer is a Paperclip secret, injected as an
Authorization header per call by resolveCredentialHeaders, and the suite
upstream already asserts such a value never lands in activity, invocation
or audit logs.
VERSION SELECTOR
Left unset, which resolves to `latest`. Do not pin it: a pinned
versionSelector silently keeps serving the old value through a rotation,
so a rotated-because-leaked bearer would go on working.
